synth.name: Init
synth.description: Default patch: detuned saw + square through a 24 dB low-pass.

synth.name: Acid Bass
synth.description: Single saw, resonant 24 dB filter with a snappy envelope and glide.

synth.name: Sub Bass
synth.description: Round sine + sub square, almost no filter movement.

synth.name: Pluck
synth.description: Short decaying saw/pulse pluck for arpeggios.

synth.name: FM Bell
synth.description: Sine carrier modulated by a sine at 3.5x: inharmonic bell. Velocity opens the FM via the envelope.

synth.name: FM E-Piano
synth.description: Sine 1:1 FM with a short bright attack (osc2 pitch envelope adds the tine "ding").

synth.name: Supersaw Lead
synth.description: 4-voice unison saws, wide stereo, slight glide.

synth.name: Sync Lead
synth.description: Osc2 hard-synced to osc1, its pitch swept by the filter envelope.

synth.name: Chiptune Square
synth.description: 12.5% pulse, no filter, instant envelopes: 8-bit console style.

synth.name: PWM Strings
synth.description: Two slowly pulse-width-modulated pulses, slow attack and release.

synth.name: Warm Pad
synth.description: Detuned triangle + saw, slow swelling filter.

synth.name: Brass
synth.description: Two saws, filter envelope with a slight attack "blat".

synth.name: Organ
synth.description: Square + octave-up square + sub, gate envelope, LFO tremolo.

synth.name: Wobble Bass
synth.description: Saw + sub through a resonant low-pass swept by a triangle LFO.

synth.name: Noise Sweep FX
synth.description: Band-passed noise riser; hold a note and let the filter envelope rise.

synth.name: Sample & Hold Blips
synth.description: Random filter steps from the S&H LFO over a resonant pulse.

synth.name: Hyper Saw
synth.description: 7 unison saws bunched around the centre pitch (supersaw), quieter outer copies, wide stereo.

synth.name: Eurobeat Arp
synth.description: Hold a chord: 1/16 up-arpeggio over 2 octaves in time with the host tempo. Short bright pluck.

synth.name: Off-beat Stabs
synth.description: Hold a chord: the Chord arpeggiator plays it on the 8th-note off-beats (rhythm gate), detuned saws.

synth.name: Pumping Pad
synth.description: Wide saw pad that ducks on every beat (synced Duck LFO on the volume), like a kick sidechain.

synth.name: Octave Legato Bass
synth.description: Mono legato saw bass: overlapping notes slide without restarting the envelope (glide only when legato).

synth.name: Chip Noise Drum
synth.description: 8-bit console style shift-register noise, short decay: pitch the note for hats (high) or snares (low).

synth.name: Chip Metal Noise
synth.description: Short-mode shift-register noise: a buzzy, metallic tone at the note pitch (8-bit bells, laser zaps).

synth.name: Rubber Mono Bass
synth.description: Rounded pulse/sub bass with a quick resonant envelope. Detached notes punch; overlaps slide.

synth.name: Reese Bass
synth.description: Detuned saw pair with a sub foundation and slow filter movement. Play single low notes.

synth.name: Hollow Pulse Lead
synth.description: Narrow pulse with triangle body and gentle PWM; mono legato for lyrical melodies.

synth.name: Soft Sine Lead
synth.description: Pure sine with a faint octave overtone, slow legato slides and mod-wheel vibrato.

synth.name: Poly Chord Stab
synth.description: Short saw/pulse chord hits without an arpeggiator. Use off-beat MIDI chords for house or pop.

synth.name: Slow Chord Wash
synth.description: Soft triangle/pulse layers, rising filter and subtle stereo drift. Release before the next large chord.

synth.name: Glass Pluck
synth.description: Octave-ratio sine FM with a short glassy transient; play individual notes or small chords.

synth.name: Dusty Keys
synth.description: Dark triangle/pulse keys with a little filtered noise and slow pitch wobble. No samples or bit crusher.

synth.name: Triplet Cascade
synth.description: Hold a chord for a descending two-octave triplet arpeggio; short pulse/triangle plucks.

synth.name: Rhythmic Steps
synth.description: Hold a chord for a swung, five-step up/down pattern with a rest on step 3. Follows host tempo.

synth.name: Ambient Hall Pad
synth.description: Slow detuned saw/triangle pad through chorus and a long, dark hall reverb.

synth.name: Chorus Strings
synth.description: One PWM pulse per note thickened by a stereo chorus (80s string machine), with a small room.

synth.name: Dotted Delay Lead
synth.description: Mono saw lead with a dotted-eighth ping-pong delay synced to the tempo, plus a little reverb.

synth.name: Ping-Pong Pluck
synth.description: Short square pluck bouncing left and right on 1/8 echoes (tempo synced); repeats get darker.

synth.name: Dub Chord
synth.description: Short filtered chord stab into a dark, long dotted-quarter delay and a spring-like small reverb.

synth.name: Vowel Choir Pad
synth.description: Two vocal-formant wavetables drifting through the vowels with a slow LFO; wide unison. Hold chords.

synth.name: Morphing Wave Lead
synth.description: Basic Shapes wavetable: each note starts square-ish and settles toward a soft triangle with the filter envelope. Legato glide.

synth.name: Harmonic Scan Pluck
synth.description: Harmonic Sweep wavetable driven by the amp envelope: the band of harmonics falls as the note decays. Notes or small chords.

synth.name: Digital Growl Bass
synth.description: Digital (8-bit XOR) wavetable scanned by an 1/8-note synced LFO over a sub; mono. Play single low notes.

synth.name: PWM Sweep Strings
synth.description: PWM Sweep wavetable on both oscillators at two pulse widths, swept together by a slow LFO: an ensemble-like string pad.

synth.name: Pressure Pad
synth.description: Slow saw pad that opens and shimmers as you press into the keys (aftertouch -> cutoff and vibrato speed); LFO 2 drifts it across the stereo field, each note a little detuned at random.

synth.name: Sync Sweep Lead
synth.description: Hard-sync lead whose sync sweep comes from the mod envelope; harder notes open the filter, aftertouch pushes the sync pitch higher (screams).

synth.name: Tempo Wobble Bass
synth.description: LFO 2 locked to 1/8 notes sweeps the cutoff (dubstep-style wobble, follows the host tempo); aftertouch adds resonance, the mod wheel adds a second, faster filter wobble from LFO 1.

synth.name: Scatter Pluck
synth.description: Every note gets its own random pan position and brightness, and a quick pitch blip from the mod envelope at the attack: lively plucked chords.

synth.name: DX E-Piano
synth.description: Glassy FM electric piano (GM EP 2): 1:1 sine FM whose index falls from bright to mellow with the mod envelope.

synth.name: String Ensemble
synth.description: Section strings: five detuned saws, slow bow-like attack, warm low-pass, chorus and a hall.

synth.name: Tremolo Strings
synth.description: The string ensemble bowed in fast tremolo (about 8 strokes per second) for tension under a cue.

synth.name: Choir Aahs
synth.description: Vocal Formants wavetable held on the "a" vowel, unison voices, gentle vibrato and a church-like reverb.

synth.name: Voice Oohs
synth.description: The choir on a closed "u" vowel: darker and softer, for backing pads.

synth.name: Orchestra Hit
synth.description: Short tutti stab: wide saws plus a fifth above, a noise burst and a big hall. Play single notes or octaves.

synth.name: Brass Section
synth.description: The Brass patch as a section: three-voice unison, chorus and a room. Play chords.

synth.name: Calliope Lead
synth.description: Steam-whistle lead: triangle plus breathy noise with a wide, quick vibrato.

synth.name: Chiff Lead
synth.description: Soft flute-like lead with a breathy "chiff" of noise at the start of every note.

synth.name: Fifths Lead
synth.description: Two saws a perfect fifth apart: every note is a power chord. Mono legato.

synth.name: Bass + Lead
synth.description: Saw lead doubled an octave down with a sub: one mono line covers both bass and melody.

synth.name: New Age Pad
synth.description: A bell-like FM ping on top of a soft swelling pad: the attack sparkles, the tail glows.

synth.name: Bowed Pad
synth.description: Glass-harmonica-like pad: slow swelling triangles with bow noise and a filter that opens as the note grows.

synth.name: Metallic Pad
synth.description: Inharmonic sine FM (3.5x) with a slow attack and chorus: a cold, shimmering metal pad.

synth.name: Rain
synth.description: Random droplets: band-passed noise whose brightness and level jump with a fast sample & hold LFO.

synth.name: Soundtrack
synth.description: Cinematic swell: dark saws slowly opening over several seconds into a long hall.

synth.name: Crystal
synth.description: High inharmonic FM pings bouncing on a ping-pong delay into reverb: icy sparkles.

synth.name: Brightness
synth.description: Very bright, wide hard-sync pad with a shimmer of reverb.

synth.name: Goblin
synth.description: Muttering creature: the vowel wavetable jumps randomly with a slow sample & hold, through a resonant filter.

synth.name: Echo Drops
synth.description: Short sine-FM drops repeating on a long dotted ping-pong delay (tempo synced).

synth.name: Sci-Fi
synth.description: FM drone whose modulator pitch is swept by two slow LFOs: bubbling spaceship computer.

synth.name: Synth Drum
synth.description: Electronic tom (Simmons-style): a sine that drops two octaves in a few tens of ms, with a click of noise. Tune with the key.

synth.name: Reverse Cymbal
synth.description: High-passed noise swelling up over 1.5 s and cut off sharply, like a cymbal played backwards. Hold the note.

synth.name: Breath Noise
synth.description: Breathing air: band-passed noise that swells in and out slowly.

synth.name: Seashore
synth.description: Waves on a beach: low-passed noise whose cutoff and level surge with a slow LFO. Hold a note.

synth.name: Bird Tweet
synth.description: Chirping bird: a high sine trilled by a fast LFO with an upward pitch flick on each note. Play high.

synth.name: Telephone Ring
synth.description: Old bell telephone: two pulse tones a third apart, chopped by a fast square tremolo.

synth.name: Helicopter
synth.description: Rotor blades: repeated low pressure thumps with a decaying air wash over a steady engine rumble. Hold a note; Noise Clock changes rotor speed, not note pitch.

synth.name: Applause
synth.description: Crowd applause: six independently timed, short hand-clap bursts with soft attacks and a room tail. Hold a note; Noise Clock changes crowd activity.

synth.name: Gunshot
synth.description: Short gunshot: a brief broadband crack, low pressure body and falling thump, with a small room tail. Each note-on fires once, even if held; Noise Clock changes playback speed.

phys.name: Nylon Guitar
phys.description: Soft plucked string: strong loop damping, warm pick, plucked away from the bridge.

phys.name: Steel String
phys.description: Bright, long-sustaining steel string picked near the bridge.

phys.name: Harp
phys.description: Plucked near the middle (fewer even harmonics), rings on after release.

phys.name: Koto-ish
phys.description: Plucked very close to the bridge with a hard pick: thin and twangy.

phys.name: Sitar
phys.description: Jawari bridge (String Sawari): the string buzzes against the curved bridge, so the bright, nasal partials keep ringing.

phys.name: Shamisen
phys.description: Hard plectrum near the bridge with a light sawari buzz; short, percussive decay.

phys.name: Hammered Dulcimer
phys.description: Hammer pulse instead of a noise burst, long ring.

phys.name: Clean Electric
phys.description: Bright steel string through a clean amp: picked near the bridge, long sustain, a little room.

phys.name: Jazz Guitar
phys.description: Warm, round archtop sound: neck-pickup-like (picked further from the bridge), tone rolled off.

phys.name: Crunch Rhythm
phys.description: Amp on the edge of breakup: chords stay clear, harder picking growls.

phys.name: Overdrive Lead
phys.description: Singing lead: overdriven, long sustain, a little vibrato and room. Use pitch bend for bends.

phys.name: Distortion Power Chord
phys.description: High-gain two-stage distortion for rock / eurobeat riffs: play root + fifth (+ octave).

phys.name: Palm Mute Chug
phys.description: Distorted strings damped right after the pick (palm mute): short, punchy 8th-note chugs.

phys.name: Marimba
phys.description: Tuned bar (modes ~1 : 3.9 : 9.2), soft-ish mallet, high modes die quickly.

phys.name: Vibraphone
phys.description: Metal bar tuned 1 : 4 : 10 with a long sustain.

phys.name: Glockenspiel
phys.description: Untuned free bar (1 : 2.76 : 5.40): the classic inharmonic shimmer.

phys.name: Wine Glass
phys.description: Glass modes, very little high damping, gently struck.

phys.name: Church Bell
phys.description: Hum / prime / tierce / quint / nominal partials, very long decay.

phys.name: Kalimba
phys.description: Plucked tine: strong fundamental, one high partial (~5.9x).

phys.name: Gamelan Gong
phys.description: Large bossed gong: deep fundamental with a slowly beating twin mode (ombak), very long decay. Play low notes.

phys.name: Bonang
phys.description: Small kettle gong of the gamelan: bright, ringing, a little beating. Good with 5-EDO (slendro-like) tuning.

phys.name: Hand Drum
phys.description: Circular membrane modes (1 : 1.59 : 2.14 ...), short decay.

phys.name: Violin
phys.description: Waveguide string driven by a stick-slip bow, bowed near the bridge, with a little vibrato.

phys.name: Cello
phys.description: Slower bow, darker bridge, slower vibrato. Play it low.

phys.name: Sul Ponticello
phys.description: Bowed very close to the bridge with light pressure: glassy, upper partials take over.

phys.name: Clarinet
phys.description: Reed + cylindrical bore: closed at one end, so mostly odd harmonics.

phys.name: Breathy Flute
phys.description: Air jet across the embouchure hole, lots of breath noise.

phys.name: Pan Pipe
phys.description: Jet driven pipe with a soft, round attack and little vibrato.

phys.name: Tom
phys.description: 2D membrane mesh struck off-centre: inharmonic drum modes appear by themselves.

phys.name: Steel Plate
phys.description: Square plate, hard strike near the corner, long ring with little high damping.

phys.name: Grand Piano
phys.description: Two detuned stiff strings per note: stretched partials, beating, long decay.

phys.name: Honky-tonk
phys.description: Badly tuned unison and a hard hammer.

phys.name: Bell-ish Strings
phys.description: Inharmonicity at maximum: the stretched partials start to sound like a bell.

phys.name: Trumpet
phys.description: Buzzing lips on a bore two periods long, bright bell, a touch of vibrato. Brighter the harder you play.

phys.name: Trombone
phys.description: Softer lips and a darker bell; play it low.

phys.name: French Horn
phys.description: Gentle lips and a hand in the bell (very dark), slow attack, bigger room.

phys.name: Flugelhorn
phys.description: Mellow: little lip buzz, soft attack, round bell.

phys.name: Muted Nylon
phys.description: Short, softly damped plucks with little room; use for intimate rhythmic picking.

phys.name: Felt Piano
phys.description: Soft hammer, damped upper partials and gentle string beating; a quiet piano texture with a small room.

phys.name: Glass Atmosphere
phys.description: Soft glass strikes with long ringing tails and a wide room. Leave space between chords.

phys.name: Pure Flute
phys.description: Low breath noise, gentle attack and restrained vibrato for clear sustained melodies.

phys.name: Expressive Violin
phys.description: The Violin with aftertouch: pressing harder digs the bow in, brightens the bridge and widens the vibrato (needs a keyboard with aftertouch, or the Pressure strip).

phys.name: Breath Trumpet
phys.description: Trumpet blown by aftertouch: soft keys start mellow, pressing in blows harder (brassier, brighter bell) and adds vibrato.

phys.name: Breath Clarinet
phys.description: Clarinet with aftertouch as breath: press in for more reed pressure and a little vibrato.

phys.name: Acoustic Bass
phys.description: Upright bass: soft finger pluck in the middle of a heavily damped string, short woody body. Play in octaves 1-2.

phys.name: Finger Bass
phys.description: Electric bass played with the fingers: round attack, long sustain through a clean amp.

phys.name: Pick Bass
phys.description: Electric bass played with a pick near the bridge: clicky, bright attack for rock lines.

phys.name: Fretless Bass
phys.description: Mellow singing bass with slow vibrato; the pitch bend spans an octave for slides.

phys.name: Slap Bass
phys.description: Thumb slap: a hard hammer strike right at the bridge end, bright and percussive, with a short decay.

phys.name: Harpsichord
phys.description: Quill plucking close to the end of a thin, lightly damped string; the damper stops it quickly on release.

phys.name: Clavinet
phys.description: Tangent strike at the very end of the string through a bright clean amp: funky, short and nasal.

phys.name: Bright Piano
phys.description: Grand piano with hard hammers and less damping of the upper partials; cuts through a mix.

phys.name: Electric Grand
phys.description: Short-stringed electric grand (CP-style): hard hammers, almost no soundboard, wider chorus-like unison, clean amp.

phys.name: Viola
phys.description: Between the violin and the cello: medium pressure, slightly darker and slower vibrato.

phys.name: Contrabass
phys.description: Arco double bass: heavy bow, slow attack and a dark tone. Play in octaves 1-2.

phys.name: Fiddle
phys.description: Folk fiddle: bright, quick bow attack and little room for dance tunes.

phys.name: Pizzicato Strings
phys.description: Plucked orchestral strings: finger pluck mid-string, short damped decay and a concert room.

phys.name: Piccolo
phys.description: Small bright flute: pure jet, quick attack and a fast light vibrato. Play an octave above the flute.

phys.name: Recorder
phys.description: Fixed windway, so a steady, almost noise-free tone with a fast attack and no vibrato.

phys.name: Shakuhachi
phys.description: Very breathy bamboo flute with a soft, slow-blooming attack and wide, slow vibrato.

phys.name: Whistle
phys.description: Tin whistle: thin, bright and pure with a lively vibrato.

phys.name: Ocarina
phys.description: Round, hollow vessel flute: centred jet (few even harmonics), very little noise, gentle vibrato.

phys.name: Blown Bottle
phys.description: Air blown across a bottle neck: lots of turbulence, low pressure and a slow swell.

phys.name: Tuba
phys.description: Big dark brass: low lip buzz, slow attack, closed bell. Play in octaves 1-2.

phys.name: Xylophone
phys.description: Hard mallets on short rosewood bars: bright, dry and quickly decaying.

phys.name: Tubular Bells
phys.description: Chimes: tubular-bell modes (the strike note an octave below the 4th mode) hit with a hard hammer, a long ring and a big room. Play in octaves 4-5.

phys.name: Celesta
phys.description: Felt hammers on small steel bars: a soft, sweet glockenspiel with a shorter tail.

phys.name: Music Box
phys.description: Plucked steel comb: kalimba-like tines, very hard and bright, lightly ringing. Play high.

phys.name: Tinkle Bell
phys.description: Small bright bell: church-bell modes, very hard strike and a short shimmer.

phys.name: Agogo
phys.description: Clanky metal cowbell: kettle-gong modes, hard stick, short decay.

phys.name: Steel Drums
phys.description: Trinidad steel pan: note areas tuned to fundamental, octave and twelfth, rubber-tipped sticks and a warm room.

phys.name: Woodblock
phys.description: Hollow wooden block: bar modes, very hard stick, almost no ring.

phys.name: Taiko
phys.description: Huge Japanese drum: large circular membrane, soft heavy beater and a hall. Play low.

phys.name: Timpani
phys.description: Kettle drum: membrane struck near the rim with a felt mallet, long pitched boom. Play in octaves 2-3.

phys.name: Soprano Sax
phys.description: Straight soprano: stiff reed, bright and focused, quick vibrato. Play in octaves 4-5.

phys.name: Alto Sax
phys.description: Alto saxophone: medium reed, some breath and a singing vibrato. Play in octaves 3-5.

phys.name: Tenor Sax
phys.description: Tenor saxophone: soft reed blown hard, breathy and husky. Play in octaves 2-4.

phys.name: Baritone Sax
phys.description: Bari sax: the softest reed and full pressure for a gruff low honk. Play in octaves 1-3.

phys.name: Oboe
phys.description: Oboe: double reed on a narrow cone, thin and nasal with a gentle vibrato. Play in octaves 4-5.

phys.name: English Horn
phys.description: Cor anglais: a darker, softer oboe a fifth lower, slower attack. Play in octaves 3-4.

phys.name: Bassoon
phys.description: Bassoon: double reed, reedy and woody, almost no vibrato. Play in octaves 2-3.

phys.name: Shanai
phys.description: Shehnai: piercing double reed, hard-blown with a wide, fast vibrato. Play in octaves 4-5.

phys.name: Drawbar Organ
phys.description: Tonewheel organ, 888000000 registration (16' 5 1/3' 8'): round and full, rotary speaker on slow. Mod wheel up = fast rotor.

phys.name: Percussive Organ
phys.description: Jazz organ: 888000000 with fast third-harmonic percussion (single trigger: play detached to re-strike) and key click, slow rotor.

phys.name: Rock Organ
phys.description: Overdriven tonewheel organ (888600000) through a crunch amp and a fast rotary speaker, loud key click.

phys.name: Gospel Organ
phys.description: All drawbars out (888888888): bright and huge, fast rotor. Mod wheel down to keep it fast; try slow rotor for chords.

phys.name: Ballad Organ
phys.description: Soft 8' + 4' (008800000) on a slow rotor, little click: pads behind a band.

phys.name: Church Organ
phys.description: Organ chorus 16' 8' 4' 2 2/3' 2' 1' without rotary or click in a big room, a slower release (stands in for a pipe organ).

phys.name: Accordion
phys.description: Musette accordion: three reeds per note, one in tune and two about 12 cents above and below, so every note shimmers. Steady bellows.

phys.name: Bandoneon
phys.description: Tango bandoneon: a single dry reed, darker and pushed harder, with a slower bellows attack.

phys.name: Harmonica
phys.description: Blues harp: one bright reed, breathy, a hand-tremolo vibrato; aftertouch blows harder. Bend range two semitones.

phys.name: Reed Organ
phys.description: Harmonium / pump organ: soft, round free reeds with a slow attack and a gentle beat between two ranks.

drums.name: 808-ish
drums.description: Long boomy kick, soft snare, metallic hats, classic cowbell.

drums.name: 909-ish
drums.description: Punchy kick with a click, bright snappy snare, noisy hats.

drums.name: Tight Lo-fi
drums.description: Short, dry and dark: everything decays fast.

drums.name: Electro Big Room
drums.description: Huge distorted kick, wide clap, long cymbals.

drums.name: Dry House
drums.description: Compact four-on-the-floor kick, crisp snare/clap and short hats; leaves room for a bass line.

drums.name: Synthwave Arena
drums.description: Deep electronic kick, broad snare/clap and ringing toms for retro pop. Synthesized tails, no gated reverb.

drums.name: Soft Percussion
drums.description: Rounded kick, dry rim and subdued cymbals with forward shaker/toms; useful for sparse arrangements.
